- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10%.
- Underestimate late-period prices (last 5–10 days of forecast) when true values show strong upward momentum; adjust upward by 3–8% for the final 10 days.
- When model shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce forecast peak by 5–15% to avoid overshoot.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecasted values before final adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless driven by strong policy or supply shock.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is >10% above forecast at day 10+, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for each subsequent day to capture momentum.
